_comment: Websites named by hand, ahead of any directory. This is the FIRST source the
tool consults and it WINS: a manual entry is a deliberate human decision and
is never overridden by TED or NocoDB. Delete an entry once TED carries the
same repository and the normal flow takes over with no code change.
businessName is also the TED join key — it is normalised (lowercased,
bracketed suffixes dropped) and matched against TED client names, which is
how a run finds the client's revision-cycle and pre-release tasks.
siteId must be stable: approvals.json, job dedupe and review links key off it.

sites.note: GitOps JSON (Model B) pilot. Named to match TED client 1397 'NUVO Aesthetics Clinic (clone)', so revisions post to task 9077 and pre-release to 9080.
PHP theme (Model A), ten client themes, currently serving g99-white-coat-aesthetics-llc. Deliberately NOT named after a TED client: it is shared infrastructure, not one client's site.
What TED client 1534 points at. Checked 2026-08-27: the repo has neither web/app/themes nor resources/site.json, so an edit will refuse until something is built there.
